summary: Orphaned NTUSER.DAT after depot restore leads to temporary profile loop on corporate Windows images
summary_detail: After depot-level disk replacement and OS restore, a subset of devices boot to a temporary user profile due to an orphaned/duplicated NTUSER.DAT and mismatched SID mapping from the restoration flow.
description: Issue summary: Several devices returned from depot repair (drive replacement + OS restore) are failing to load the user's roaming profile and instead log users into a temporary profile. Affected employees report missing desktop icons, settings, and Outlook reconfiguration. Impact: Productivity loss for impacted users; increased manual support time for SOC/IT to reattach correct profile HIVE and rehydrate settings. Initial triage shows NTUSER.DAT present in C:\Users\<username> but the registry hive that should be loaded during logon is not matching the expected SID in HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows NT\CurrentVersion\ProfileList. Hypothesis: Depot restore process re-applied an image but did not reconcile previous profile SIDs when restoring files from backup (vendor restores user files by SID or username), leading to duplicate NTUSER.DAT files or a mismatched ACL that prevents Profile Service from loading the hive. This differs from standard 'temporary profile due to corrupt registry' because NTUSER.DAT files exist and show correct timestamps from depot transfer.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Depot repair: replace NVMe and perform vendor OS restore (image + file restore) on a corporate asset.
2) Re-enroll device into Intune/AAD and run provisioning tasks (join, SCCM baseline, apply profile redirection).
3) Have a user sign in with corporate credentials.
4) Observe Windows logs and the user being signed into a TEMP profile ("Temporary Profile" banner) and missing profile settings.
expected_result: After depot restore and re-enrollment, user signs in to their existing roaming/cached profile with desktop and Outlook settings preserved.
actual_result: Sign-in succeeds but user gets a temporary profile. C:\Users\<username> contains NTUSER.DAT files that do not match SID-to-profile mapping in registry, or NTUSER.DAT is locked/unreadable by Profile Service.
logs: EventLog: Application - User Profile Service - EventID 1505: Windows cannot load the user profile for the local account.
EventLog: System - EventID 6005/6006 around boot correlates with profile load failures.
SCCM inventory: File hash shows two NTUSER.DAT variants: NTUSER.DAT and NTUSER.DAT.bak with different ACLs (SYSTEM and BUILTIN\Administrators have full control on one, but not on the other).
Tooling output: `reg load` attempts fail with STATUS_ACCESS_DENIED when run under service account context; manual load using SYSTEM via psexec succeeds indicating ACL mismatch.
investigation_notes: 03/05 - Emily: Initial report from desktop support (Slack #it-support) about 6 units in a single depot batch showing temporary profile loop. Ticket opened.

03/06 - Imaging team: Confirmed depot vendor uses file-level restore tied to username rather than SID. Vendor restore process creates NTUSER.DAT in target path but ownership set to original SID which is not present on rejoined AAD devices.

03/07 - Security: Confirmed no credential exposure; files were restored from vendor backup with preserved ACLs. ACL mismatch prevents Profile Service from loading hive as the registry identity differs on new AAD device.

03/08 - Workaround validated: Boot to WinRE, take ownership of NTUSER.DAT, set ACL to allow SYSTEM and Administrators read/write, then reboot – Profile Service loads hive and user signs in normally. Manual but repeatable.

03/09 - Engineering: Confirmed correlation with depot restore flow where vendor's tool preserves NTFS ACLs (including SIDs that do not exist on re-enrolled devices) — leads to orphaned files that are unreadable by local SYSTEM account until ownership fixed.

03/09 - Hypothesis: Two failure modes present: (a) restored NTUSER.DAT owned by old SID -> access denied, (b) restored NTUSER.DAT content is for different user -> SID mismatch in ProfileList -> temporary profile.
comments: Emily Zhang (03/05): Reported initial user cases - ticket created. Logged sample device serials and user principals.
Marco Silva (03/06): Requesting vendor depot batch ID and zdrive image manifest. Assigned to imaging component.
Imaging Vendor (03/07): Confirm vendor tool preserves file ACLs by design; default behavior documented in external runbook: link: https://vendor.example.com/runbook/restore-acls
Security (03/08): Confirm manual ownership change is safe for these artifacts; recommended patch process to remove stale SIDs during restore.
Support Lead (03/09): Approved emergency interim script to run post-restore (takeown + icacls reset) — script staged in internal repo PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/it-scripts/pull/128
Marco Silva (03/10): Requesting Ops to schedule mandated post-depot job and notifying vendor to change default behavior.
resolution: Workaround: Implemented a post-depot remediation script that runs on first boot after vendor restore: it takes ownership of C:\Users\*\NTUSER.DAT if ACL contains unknown SIDs, resets ACL to grant SYSTEM and Administrators full control, and notifies device contact. This resolves TEMP profile loop for 95% of reported cases. Permanent fix: vendor agreed to update restore workflow to map/translate SIDs to target device local accounts or strip ACLs during file restore. Engineering created a follow-up task to add an automated check into the provisioning pipeline to detect orphaned ACLs before letting devices leave depot.
postmortem_action_items: 1) Imaging: Add `icacls` remediation step to post-restore job (priority P1) - due 2026-03-20.
2) Vendor SLAs: Vendor to change default restore behavior to strip/translate ACLs or run our remediation (contract amendment logged) - vendor commit received 2026-03-09.
3) Automation: Create a pre-enrollment gating check in SCCM/Intune autopilot to scan C:\Users for orphaned ACLs and remediate automatically - ticket INT-389010 created.
4) KB: Publish internal runbook for SOC/Desktop to recover affected users manually (reg load + icacls steps) - Confluence page linked below.
